items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: the first things that hit me were those boogie woogie things of Pete Johnson. I’d go oh my God, this is so cool

ctx.x: My name is Monk Rowe and I am in the office in Buffalo of Chuck Mancuso. And I’m glad to be here at Buffalo State College. And I’m going to describe you as, well first of all, a professor of music, but researcher and author, and a huge fan — is that where it started, as being a huge fan — of this music?

Yeah, right. It started back in the 50s, and I was just a kid playing a lot of sports and I thought I was going to be a sports writer. And I found out that this great music that I loved — you know my father had these 78s, and when we were little kids both mom and dad worked, and so they’d say on Saturday mornings you’ve got to be quiet, because we’re upstairs sleeping in the house. So I went through his records. I mean I was what, maybe nine, ten years old. And the first things that hit me were those boogie…
